info.title: Bookrail API
info.description:
Booking infrastructure: availability, holds, bookings, their life cycle, and the events they emit.

This document is **generated** from the Zod schemas of the server and proved by a contract guard that
validates every response of the test suite against the schema declared here. In case of a disagreement
between this file and any prose documentation, this file is right.

- Every instant is ISO 8601. Any explicit offset is accepted on input; every instant is returned in UTC.
- Identifiers are prefixed (`bk_`, `res_`, `svc_`, …); the prefix says what the object is.
- Lists are cursored: `?limit=&starting_after=`, never an offset, and never a total.
- Every `POST /v1/...` honours `Idempotency-Key`. The same key within 24 hours replays the same response.

tags.name: locations
tags.description: Physical places, each with a time zone.

tags.name: resources
tags.description: What a booking consumes: a person, a room, a court, a piece of equipment.

tags.description: Interchangeable resources, with an allocation strategy.

tags.name: services
tags.description: What a customer books, with its durations, buffers, price and requirements.

tags.description: Cancellation, reschedule, no-show and confirmation rules.

tags.name: customers
tags.description: The people bookings are made for.

tags.name: holds
tags.description: Capacity taken for a few minutes, before it becomes a booking.

tags.name: bookings
tags.description: The booking and its life cycle.

tags.name: events
tags.description: The append-only log of everything that happened.

tags.name: webhooks
tags.description: Delivery endpoints, their signing secret and their delivery log.

environment.description: The environment of the API key that created the object.

event_type.description: Type of the event this delivery carries. Joined in by the listing and by `/test`; absent from the answer of `/retry`.
